summary: R1, R2, R3 and R5 are resolved. R4's apparatus and field-symbol explanations are semantically correct and match the reused bound figure context, but the new Figure 159 explanation splits one sentence across authoritative paragraphs 17 and 18, ending the former with a semicolon and starting the latter with lowercase plain. This affected child-readability defect requires a prose-only repair. Source, equations, numbers, references, unrelated bytes and all three boundary anchors pass the bounded preservation checks.

findingConclusions.sourceConclusion: The original source_text, section-mark reference and formulas remain exact. The added premises explain the retained ideal-model derivation rather than replacing source quantities or asserting an erratum.
findingConclusions.scienceConclusion: Equal amounts of opposite plate charge and no added external field are now explicit. Under the retained broad-plate, homogeneous linear ideal-medium assumptions, the contributions in the gap have equal strength and the same positive-to-negative direction, hence each is half the total. The text does not apply this half-field premise to unmatched charges or an external field.
findingConclusions.noviceConclusion: Charge signs, conducting, insulating, field, energy and single-plate charge amount now have local explanations. The reader is told what is equal, what is opposite and why the contributions add without having to consult the retained section 81 reference.
findingConclusions.limits: Conditional approval of these explanatory statements in the stated ideal model, not approval of real dielectric material-mechanical effects.

findingConclusions.sourceConclusion: The force-work expression, voltage replacement, equation (8-42) and reference (8-22) retain their exact source math tokens. Blocks 4 and 5 remain byte-preserved under the checked baseline projection.
findingConclusions.scienceConclusion: The text labels the movement an ideal thought experiment, holds one plate still and lets the other approach along the attraction. At fixed charge, area and maintained ideal material conditions, the force remains constant and equals single-plate charge amount times the other plate's half-field. The full distance is the initial gap d; the ideal zero-gap limit is explicitly the zero of stored field energy, so full positive field work equals initial energy. Interaction is counted once. Mechanical reversal restores the energy at fixed charge and is explicitly distinguished from electrical charging. The reversible negligible-loss charging, supply exchange and fixed-voltage circuit-loss caveats remain sound and are not replaced by a universal loss fraction.
findingConclusions.noviceConclusion: Force times full distance, the zero-energy reference, movement direction, symbol meanings and the verbal Ed-to-voltage replacement are now available locally. The child is not asked to infer full initial energy from an arbitrary partial displacement or count the same interaction twice.
findingConclusions.limits: The zero-gap argument is an ideal limit, not actual conductor contact through a physical dielectric or a capacitor-handling procedure. No unrestricted equality between fixed-voltage supply energy and stored energy is approved.

findingConclusions.sourceConclusion: References (8-36), (8-42) and (8-43), and every original mathematical token, remain unchanged. U and V are explained in prose as labels for the same potential-difference quantity; neither source symbol is substituted.
findingConclusions.scienceConclusion: The local charge-amount/voltage-size definition gives the two correct replacements: multiplying charge amount by itself and dividing by capacitance and two, or multiplying capacitance by voltage size twice and dividing by two. These are explicitly the same stored energy, not energies to sum. The retained fixed linear, negligible-loss capacitance scope excludes an unrestricted nonlinear-device claim.
findingConclusions.noviceConclusion: The meanings of division and squaring, both substitution steps and the reason that q squared or V squared appears are stated in words. The child need not retrieve the earlier equation or perform an unstated algebraic rearrangement.
findingConclusions.limits: Approval is of the local explanatory bridge to the unchanged formulas, not an extension to voltage-dependent, hysteretic or lossy capacitors.

findingConclusions.sourceConclusion: Both unchanged figure objects and English captions remain exact against the first reviewed draft. The added apparatus and field descriptions agree with the first review's unchanged bound textual figure context. No label, drawing, shared N80 context or source figure reference is changed.
findingConclusions.scienceConclusion: The Leyden jar's inner/outer metal coatings and separating glass are correctly identified. Figure 159's left-negative/right-positive signs, charge-magnitude bars, positive-to-negative leftward total-field arrows and directional accent are explained. The total field depicted is explicitly distinguished from the other plate's half-field used for force. A possible discharge is not asserted to be a visible spark in the drawing.
findingConclusions.noviceConclusion: The semantic bridge is supplied, but the direction-versus-size sentence is broken across two actual paragraphs. Paragraph 17 ends with a semicolon after size, and paragraph 18 starts with lowercase plain. This is not a soft wrap: both the draft's blank-line separator and the independently recomputed authoritative outline confirm two paragraphs. It repeats the kind of unfinished-sentence carryover that the first R5 rejected, now inside the newly affected figure explanation.
